proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the right to alienate, consume, or destroy the res—one of the three classical sticks of Roman dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). As a right, it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in a property-holder; it is externally grounded in the legal system's recognition of ownership (hence Role rather than Disposition). It is best modeled as a subclass of the existing working:LegalRight, which is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role). It is a class because 'Abusus' denotes a kind of right, not a specific instance.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of legal right (specifically a property right component), so it subclasses the existing working:LegalRight (BFO_0000023).
Redundantly explicit typing: Abusus is a Role (BFO_0000023), the right being externally grounded in juridical recognition of ownership under Roman law.

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished from the other components of dominium (Usus, Fructus)? If so, shall we mint sibling classes Usus and Fructus under LegalRight, and a parent class RomanPropertyRight or Dominium to group them?
Is the bearer of Abusus always a human person (natural person), a legal person, or either? This affects whether we need a PersonInPropertyOwnerRole or similar individual-level pattern.

Should Abusus be treated as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Role (BFO_0000023), on the grounds that the capacity to alienate or destroy the thing is grounded in the internal nature of the ownership relation rather than external social recognition? The Role typing was chosen because Roman law grounds it in juridical status, but this is contestable.

Do you want to model a specific Roman-law individual (e.g., a particular statute or jurist's text like the Corpus Iuris Civilis) as the generically dependent continuant that specifies Abusus, analogous to how USConstitution is modeled?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus (ius abutendi) names the right of the owner to alienate, consume, or destroy the owned thing—one of the three classical components of Roman dominium alongside usus (use) and fructus (enjoyment of fruits). In BFO terms, a right is a specifically dependent continuant because it inheres in a bearer (the property-holder) and depends on that bearer for its existence. Among specifically dependent continuants, it is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023) rather than a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because its ground is external: it is conferred by juridical recognition within a legal system rather than arising from the intrinsic physical or causal structure of the bearer. The existing working class LegalRight is already typed as BFO_0000023 and represents exactly this category, so Abusus is minted as a new subclass of LegalRight. It is modeled as a class (not an individual) because 'Abusus' picks out a kind or type of right that can be instantiated in many bearers across time, not a single token right. Several open questions remain: whether to also mint Usus and Fructus as sibling classes, whether the Role vs. Disposition choice is correct for this domain, and whether a specific Roman legal text should be linked as the GDC that specifies this right.
